issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Animal.name: the problem statement (text) explicitly instructs students to use a StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute, but the reference solution implements the field as a String. This mismatch (problem text vs solution code) creates ambiguity for students about which type to implement and leads to incompatible constructor/getter/setter expectations between solution/tests and the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and reference solution consistent. Option A (preferred if teaching StringBuilder is intended): change the solution's Animal class field to 'private StringBuilder name;', update the constructor to accept a String (or StringBuilder) and initialize the StringBuilder (e.g. this.name = new StringBuilder(name)), and update getName()/setName() to operate on StringBuilder (or provide getName() returning String and setName(String) delegating to the StringBuilder). Update any tests to expect the new type/behavior. Option B: if StringBuilder was an accidental suggestion, update the problem text (and UML) to request a String name to match the provided solution and tests.

issues.description: Field de.tum.cit.ase.Animal.name (internal contradiction in the problem statement): the UML diagram in the problem statement lists Animal.name as type 'String', while the textual instructions (several lines later) instruct students to use a 'StringBuilder' for the name attribute. These two statements in the problem statement contradict each other and will confuse students about the expected type.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the internal inconsistency in the problem statement: either update the UML to show 'name: StringBuilder' to match the textual instruction, or change the textual instruction to require a String. Prefer updating the UML to StringBuilder if the exercise aims to teach using StringBuilder; otherwise change the text to request a String and remove the StringBuilder reference.
